title: Short Grant Cycles vs Long-Horizon Research
bottleneck: Standard grants run 3-5 years, forcing researchers to promise deliverables on timelines suited to incremental work. Ambitious programs — new instruments, longitudinal studies, foundational theory — need decade-scale stable support that project-grant systems rarely provide. The mismatch pushes researchers toward conservative, short-payoff projects even when they recognize the distortion.
why_it_blocks: Short horizons bias the entire research portfolio toward quick, publishable results and away from the slow work that historically produced revolutions. Entire classes of ambitious research become unfundable, not through rejection but through self-censorship.
current_state: A few long-horizon funders exist (HHMI investigators, Wellcome Leap), but they cover a tiny fraction of global research spending. Endowed investigator-style awards that fund people rather than projects are the main counterexample, covering few researchers.

sources.title: Evidence and the Design and Reform of Scientific Institutions (Nintil)
